extracted.intended_audience: IP statisticians, policy makers, IP office analysts, researchers and practitioners working with industrial design and trademark statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, metrics and methodological guidance for compiling and interpreting industrial design (and related trademark) statistical indicators worldwide. Covers counts (applications, designs, registrations), classification (resident/non-resident, equivalent counts), procedural indicators (examiners, pendency, outcomes) and caveats for cross-office comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application design count (designs contained in applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics based on the number of designs contained in industrial design applications – known as application design counts – intended to improve comparability worldwide by harmonizing data from offices that allow more than one design in an application with those that allow only one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use application design counts when offices allow multiple designs per application to ensure comparability across offices with different filing systems. Report growth and totals on a design-count basis rather than raw application counts when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design count (designs per application vs per registration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of distinct designs contained in an application or registration; some offices allow more than one design per application while others allow only one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing offices, distinguish between application counts and design counts. Compare 'designs contained in applications' for harmonized measures; compare application counts only when offices' single/multiple design policies are equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent design count (regional-office multiplier approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designs in applications filed at regional offices are treated as equivalent to multiple designs in applications filed in the member states of those regional offices by multiplying each design by the number of member states (e.g., OAPI=17, BOIP=3, EUIPO=28). ARIPO is handled differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the member-state multiplier to translate regional office filings into equivalent counts for comparisons by origin. Note ARIPO exception: ARIPO does not register industrial designs with automatic region-wide applicability; count rules for ARIPO differ (see ARIPO-specific guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs Non-resident classification (office data vs origin data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications received by offices from resident and non-resident applicants are referred to as office data; applications filed by applicants at their home office (resident applications) or at foreign offices (applications abroad) are referred to as origin data (based on residence of the first named applicant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both office-level (resident/non-resident at an office) and origin-level (residence of applicant) statistics to capture filing flows. Indicate which perspective is used when presenting counts and growth rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hague System / Hague international applications (designs in international filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and trends for Hague international applications and the number of designs contained in those applications, and designation patterns by member (e.g., EU and selected members).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Hague counts separately as they reflect international filings via the Hague System. Report origin and designated-member breakdowns; highlight notable shifts (e.g., top users, growth rates by origin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and registration design counts by Locarno class and industry sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of designs by Locarno classes (32 classes) and grouping into 12 industry sectors to highlight which classes/sectors dominate filings (e.g., furnishings, clothing, packages and containers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Locarno classes and sector groupings to analyze sectoral concentration and compare top-three sector shares across offices/origins. Report top classes and their percentage shares of world totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration design counts and registrations in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of designs in registrations (registrations issued) and registrations in force (active registrations) at offices; includes totals and office rankings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting registrations in force, indicate approximate rights duration (e.g., generally up to 15 years from filing) and provide office-level shares and trends. Distinguish between newly registered designs and those currently in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of active registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The average age (in years) of industrial design registrations in force at an office (e.g., France 11.1 years, China 2.9 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use average age to describe the maturity of an office's registration stock; compare across offices noting that differences reflect both filing history and retention/renewal patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration class count by office and by origin / Madrid designation counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of registration classes recorded by office and by origin, including Madrid international registrations and equivalent registration class counts by origin. Data completeness may vary across offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that some offices report only Madrid designation data, leading to incomplete registration class counts by office and origin. Flag incomplete data and indicate when Madrid-only reporting affects totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural outcome and workflow metrics (office procedural data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office-level procedural metrics including: total applications processed; registered; partial rejections; total rejections; withdrawn or abandoned; applications pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories to summarize examination outcomes. When comparing offices, exercise caution due to procedural differences and possible omissions from offices' reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners (FTE) and staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of examiners measured in full-time equivalents (FTE) assigned to industrial design examination at an office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report examiner counts in FTE to allow comparisons of human resources across offices; note that FTE definitions may vary and impact comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency times: First office action and final decision (days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average elapsed days from filing to first office action and from filing to final office decision for industrial design applications at an office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report pendency as two benchmarks (first action, final decision). Use these to assess timeliness; caution that procedural differences make direct comparisons difficult. Provide office-specific values and explain methodological caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potentially pending applications and distribution of examination outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators such as potentially pending applications and the distribution (percentages) of examination outcomes for selected offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present potentially pending counts alongside outcome distributions to indicate workload and backlog. Clarify definitions used to compute 'potentially pending' for each office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design counts adjusted by population and GDP (per-capita and per-GDP unit metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident application design count per million population and resident application design count per USD 100 billion of GDP to compare filing intensity across origins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use per-capita and per-GDP adjustments to compare filing intensity across countries/origins. Report both metrics as complementary; interpret differences in light of economic size and population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data comparability caveats and office-specific counting changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Caveats about comparability: offices use different concepts and definitions; procedural differences hinder full harmonization; specific example: China’s 2017 application count change (from including all received applications to only those for which the office has received necessary application fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always document office-specific definition changes, reporting gaps (.. indicates not available, n.a. not applicable), and any known breaks in series. Exercise caution when computing world totals or year-on-year growth if a major office changed counting methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability and notation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Notation conventions used in the tables and text: 'n.a.' indicates not applicable; '..' indicates not available. Source attribution: WIPO Statistics Database and data collection methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the notation conventions when interpreting tables. Cite data source and data vintage (e.g., WIPO Statistics Database, September 2020). Indicate when totals are WIPO estimates covering a given number of IP offices.
